notes: The circuit image shows no breadboard; the parts list names 2 mini breadboards. I used one breadboard (bb1) only as the junction for the two 4.7 kΩ pull-up resistors and the I2C lines. Mini breadboards are not in the catalogue, so I used the catalogue breadboard type.

The image shows the two I2C lines and the 3V line sharing nodes with the resistors, with no wire drawn between the boards' A4 pins. I therefore routed A4 (SDA) and A5 (SCL) from both boards to a shared breadboard column each.
Each pull-up resistor goes from its I2C line to 3V3 from the reader board. 3V3 is distributed over the breadboard top power rail (tp), so tp.1, tp.2 and tp.3 are one strip.
Boards are 3.3 V logic, so the pull-ups go to 3V3 and not 5 V.
The manual calls A4 SDA and A5 SCL (the text says SDA on A4 and SCL on A5). The graph connects A4 to A4 and A5 to A5.
The two USB cables go to the computer for power and serial. The computer is not modelled.
The Arduino Nano 33 IoT is new to the catalogue. The 3V pin in the diagram is named 3V3.
The built-in LED is on the reader board and needs no external parts. No external LED circuit is listed.
